reel.name: Memory Tax — Paper Breakdown, Day 1
reel.scriptStatus: Script APPROVED verbatim by Vishnu 2026-11-02 01:34 CST — 83 words
reel.voice: Helio (avocado_v2:MAI_03), single pass, fixed speed 85 — final 36.84s / 135.2 wpm, measured

beats.name: Hook — two paths
beats.voiceover: Your AI agent remembers everything. Or does it? When it rewrites your history into neat memory, it can quietly drop the detail you needed.

startFrame.desc: Pic 1 full frame: diamond node top-centre, intact teal stack left, gapped slate stack right, navy background.

endFrame.desc: Pic 1 pushed in and panned left: intact teal stack fills the frame, gapped right stack sliding out of frame.

camera.to: Scale 1.22, panned to the intact left stack
camera.distance: Full frame to close on left stack

character.move: No Kit in this build; the camera move is the host motion

beats.treatment: Kinetic Remotion: full-frame push-in + pan, parallax overlay layer moving opposite to the camera
beats.notes: Overlay changes once at the 'Or does it?' turn. Frame itself travels the whole beat — not a slow zoom alone: scale + pan + parallax overlay.

beats.name: Result — bars fall
beats.voiceover: In one long-memory test, plain retrieval scored eighty-one percent, beating every fancy memory system in that test.

startFrame.desc: Pic 2 pushed in on the left: tallest teal bar dominates, shorter bars cropped right.

endFrame.desc: Pic 2 pulled back and panned right: all five descending bars visible, dots falling above the shorter bars.

camera.direction: Back and right across the bars
camera.distance: Close on tallest bar to full chart

character.move: No Kit in this build; the camera move is the host motion

beats.treatment: Kinetic Remotion: full-frame pull-back + pan, 81.4% overlay pops at 'eighty-one percent'
beats.notes: Cut (not morph) from Pic 1 to Pic 2 — different compositions; a morph would smear stacks into bars. The camera travel inside the beat is the motion.

beats.name: Payoff — the scale tips
beats.voiceover: That is the memory tax. Rewriting helps sometimes, but it costs you evidence.

startFrame.desc: Pic 3 pushed in on the scale: bright small pan left, larger grey pan right, beam level.

endFrame.desc: Pic 3 panned to the right pan: grey cluster low, beam tipped, amber arrow entering frame bottom-right.

camera.from: Full Pic 3, scale 1.00, centred on scale
camera.to: Scale 1.20, panned to the tipping right pan
camera.direction: Forward and right, following the tip
camera.distance: Full scale to close on tipping pan

character.move: No Kit in this build; the camera move is the host motion

beats.treatment: Kinetic Remotion: full-frame push-in + pan, 'Memory tax' overlay on the tipping pan
beats.notes: Sub-beat 3a of Beat 3. Same image as 3b, different camera window and overlay — that is the split that stops the 18.7s beat sitting static.

beats.name: Fix + CTA — return to the source
beats.voiceover: The fix is simple: let memory organise, but never delete the source. So keep a way back to the raw history. Follow for a new AI paper every day.
beats.overlay: Keep the source — Follow for a new AI paper every day

startFrame.desc: Pic 3 pulled back, panned down-right: amber return arrow sweeping across the lower frame.

endFrame.desc: Pic 3 pushed in on the return target: intact teal stack with organised layer on top, arrow completing its loop.

camera.to: Scale 1.18, panned to the intact stack and arrow loop
camera.direction: Back, then forward down-right along the arrow

character.move: No Kit in this build; the camera move is the host motion

beats.treatment: Kinetic Remotion: full-frame camera travel along the arrow, overlay swaps from 'Keep the source' to the Follow CTA
beats.notes: Sub-beat 3b of Beat 3. Overlay swap + camera travel, not a held still. CTA is the approved script's final sentence, verbatim.

notes.author: Director
notes.text: Image-led build per the Phase B task: the 3 approved Claude keyframes are the visuals, animated kinetically in Remotion. No Kit character is rendered in this build, so the character track is marked none on every beat rather than promising a host the video does not contain.

notes.author: Director
notes.text: Beat-to-beat transitions are cuts, not morphs: Pic 1 (stacks), Pic 2 (bars), Pic 3 (scale) are different compositions, and a first-last morph would smear one into the other. Motion lives inside each beat (full-frame scale + pan + parallax overlay). The Kling/Higgsfield first-last upgrade, if Vishnu approves it separately, is a different visual route and is NOT this build.

notes.author: Director
